title: Sam Parr: Why he bootstrapped Hampton instead of raising VC, and how he designs a business around a rich life
summary: Sam Parr explains why he chose not to raise venture capital for Hampton, how he reverse-engineers a business from constraints (Ikigai plus email CPM math), and why aligning co-founders on lifestyle non-negotiables up front matters. He also covers prioritizing audience over advertisers, protecting community quality, and timing exits for liquidity.

principles.text: Bootstrapping fits founders who want freedom and money for themselves; VC fits those who want to go huge. Pick deliberately.
principles.quote: My thought is if your main goal is freedom and like making money for yourself, bootstrapping is 100% the way to go.

principles.text: Your cap table is one of the few business mistakes you can't undo; raising money commits you to optimizing for investor returns.
principles.quote: there's basically like only maybe one or two mistakes in business that you can't undo, and your cap table's one of them.

principles.text: Choose a business model that doesn't need outside capital: charge up front and use that cash to improve the product.
principles.quote: we purposely picked like a business model where we didn't need to raise money. And so, the constraint was, we don't want to raise money, so what can we do without raising money?

principles.text: Design a business from hard constraints: market CPM, your skills, what you love, and what the world will pay for.
principles.quote: it's what's the world want, what's the world willing to pay for, what am I good at, what do I love doing? And you get something right in the middle.

principles.text: Get specific about your ideal life with co-founders up front, including what you won't sacrifice, before building together.
principles.quote: Okay, we are unwilling to sacrifice family time. Okay, cool. So, if we I'm I'm on board with that, he's on board with that.

principles.text: Prioritize your core audience over advertisers; it costs revenue short term but earns more long term.
principles.quote: I think you ultimately do make more in the end if you are like appeal to a very particular type of person.
